title: The pro-étale direct image for all finite-Tor objects
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}$, and the algebraically closed field
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes with
$\dim X\leq d$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$ be a bounded
constructible complex of $A$-modules on the small pro-étale site with
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, both notions being the intrinsic ones of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $Rf_*K$ is bounded
constructible on $Y_{\Proet}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$. That is, clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary holds at
the finite coefficient stage $A$ for *every* object of
$D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$, with no restriction to the objects of étale
origin.

proof.text: Since $K$ is intrinsically bounded constructible, clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], applied to $T=X$ and the same finite coefficient ring $A$, supplies $K'\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$ and an isomorphism $e:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_X^*K'$. In particular $K'$ is bounded below. This uses the equivalence for derived constructible complexes, not merely the equivalence for individual sheaves.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: every bounded constructible complex is of etale origin; Stacks Tags 09AK and 09AL (proetale.tex, lemma-compare-constructible and lemma-compare-constructible-derived).

proof.text: The prime $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ and $Y$, since both are schemes over the characteristic-$p$ field $k$ and $\ell\ne p$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] applies to $K$, $K'$ and $e$: its required bounded-below hypothesis on $K'$ was checked in step 1. It gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for $K'$ on the etale site, with the same constant coefficient ring $A$.

Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] to $f$ and $K'$. Its hypotheses are exactly the finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, separated finite-type morphism $f$, source dimension bound $\dim X\le d$, bounded constructibility from step 1, and Tor interval from step 2. Thus $L:=Rf_{\Et,*}K'$ is bounded constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ with Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$. No properness or separatedness of the structure morphism of $X$ is added.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: etale direct-image corollary; its vanishing and Tor-amplitude inputs remain dependencies of that corollary.

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses for the direct-image comparison. Finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separatedness means that the relative diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] makes $\Delta_f$ proper. By the definition of proper in [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\Delta_f$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Therefore $f$ is quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. This proves both comparison hypotheses from assumptions actually present in the item.

source.place: Proof, sentence preceding the direct-image comparison display: qcqs check, with quasi-separatedness justified using separatedness.
Proof, displayed direct-image comparison; Stacks Tag 09A6 (proetale.tex, lemma-morphism-comparison), in the comparison section Tag 099R cited by the dependency.

proof.text: Apply clause (i) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] on $T=Y$ to the bounded constructible etale complex $L$ and its interval $[a,b+2d]$. It follows that $\nu_Y^*L$ is intrinsically bounded constructible and has that Tor interval. The isomorphism in step 5 transfers both properties to $Rf_{\Proet,*}K$: cohomology sheaves of isomorphic derived objects are isomorphic, and for every degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $M$, tensoring that isomorphism gives isomorphic cohomology sheaves for their derived tensor products with $M$. Thus the bounded constructibility condition of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and every required vanishing in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] hold. This proves the assertion for the original arbitrary intrinsic object $K$.
